_comment: Canonical source of truth for turva.dev volatile facts. Edit here, then mirror to the surfaces that state these facts (turva-worker/src/worker.ts, README.md, the turva-mcp worker and its README, and the erekola profile README), then run: node tools/verify.mts  (add --live on a networked machine to GET the fixed list of declared surfaces in the live block of the script and verify the manifest signatures).
_eurUsdcComment: Added 2026-09-06. The USDC amount of the three x402 offers is derived from the euro price at this rate. The rate used to be baked into the finished number only: no served surface and no code comment named it, and its date lived in a private decision log. It is here now, and verify.mts recomputes every X402_MANIFEST amount from these two fields, so the rate has one copy and the gate is its reader. measuredAt is the day the rate was read. It does not move by itself, and the offer's own price note states the rate and its date.
_bundledComment: Added 2026-08-31 (Tek-317). Implementation of exactly what a diagnosis lists, sold ONLY together with that diagnosis. These are deliberately NOT in prices/services: verify.mts binds a priced service to a price key one to one, and a service listed there is a thing an agent can buy on its own. These add-ons cannot be bought on their own, so they are declared on the catalog surfaces (HOME_JSON, A2A services, WebMCP get_services, llms.txt, the services skill) with their requires field, and they are absent from the checkout surfaces (ACP_SERVICES, x402, AP2/MPP/UCP) on purpose. verify.mts reads this list, so it is the only copy.

bundledImplementation.name: Audit fix implementation
bundledImplementation.scope: Exactly the fixes the audit report lists.

_quotedAddOnsComment: Added 2026-11-08 (Tek-784). Add-ons to the audit that carry no list price: the price is quoted for each written scope, so the machine value is the string on request and never a number. They are deliberately NOT in services and NOT in bundledImplementation: services lists what an agent can buy on its own, and bundledImplementation lists fixed-price add-ons whose amounts verify.mts compares with the checkout surfaces. A quoted add-on cannot be bought on its own, so it is declared on the catalog surfaces (HOME_JSON, A2A services, the MCP server card, the get_services answers of turva-mcp and WebMCP) with its requires field, and it is absent from the checkout surfaces (ACP_SERVICES, x402, AP2/MPP/UCP, the openapi purchase paths), from the schema.org OfferCatalog and from the llms.txt Pricing list on purpose. verify.mts reads this list, so it is the only copy.

quotedAddOns.name: Active security testing
quotedAddOns.scope: Tests the agent surfaces the audit reads, or your own AI agent or web application where the written scope says so, with GLM 5.3 and Burp Suite Professional for web traffic, and starts only after you sign a written authorization.

_channelsComment: Added 2026-08-16 (Tek-238). The contact channels are declared on many surfaces (footer, JSON-LD sameAs, agent manifests, profile READMEs) and were compared to nothing: only prices had a home here. A channel that is renamed, retired or mistyped on one surface and not another is exactly the drift facts.json exists to stop, and it is the same defect class as the three-versus-four priced services. verify.mts reads this list, so it is the only copy and the gate is its reader.
_identityRefsComment: Separate from channels on purpose, and the split was found by the gate rather than designed: the first version of the sameAs check assumed every sameAs entry is a contact channel, and it immediately failed on these two. They are identity references, not places to reach a person. There are TWO Wikidata items on purpose and they are not a typo for each other: Q140276251 is turva.dev the organization and Q140276321 is Erik Rekola the person, verified on Wikidata 2026-08-16. An independent review read the pair as drift, which is exactly why both are declared here by name. sameAs is the union of the two lists, and keeping them apart is what lets the gate say which kind of entry an addition is.

isitagentready._categoryScoreComment: The score field was added 2026-08-30. measuredAt moved from 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-30 the same day as its own change and its own deploy, because the date is mirrored on five published surfaces (worker.ts in three places, the HOME_JSON lastVerified field, README.md and docs/agent-readiness.md). Behind the date are three independent runs on the same day, and all three gave exactly what 2026-08-20 gave: Level 5/5 and every category full. So the number did not change, it was measured again, and the page's own text says that a new run is a new measurement and not a confirmation of the old one. Before that, every surface repeated the TOTAL score in every category, and the gate checked it with a line that required cell.val === iar.score. That holds only while everything passes. THE VALUE IS A SCORE OUT OF A HUNDRED, NOT CHECKS OUT OF CHECKS, and that is forced and not chosen: the scanner reports a different DENOMINATOR on its public page than on its MCP interface (commerce 5/5 against 4/4, api/auth 9 against 8), but the SHARE is the same in both, since 9/9 and 8/8 are each 100. The form 100/100 was chosen because the home page table already uses it. The field checks does not return: it is the number of checks, and verify.mts fails the run if it appears.

isitagentready._surfaceWordingComment: Added 2026-08-16. On three surfaces the gate OWNED the wording: the sentence shape was hardcoded in tools/verify.mts and read from nowhere, so verify.mts was both the rule and the only record of the rule. Published wording belongs next to the published data, the same way category.label does. verify.mts now reads these fields and fails if one is missing, so this is not a second copy of a value: it is the only copy, and the gate is the reader.

security._measuredAtComment: measuredAt is the date of the Internet.nl runs, the website test and the email test. It is not the latest date of all scanners: Hardenize has its own measuredAt below and may be newer. Each Internet.nl block repeats its own measuredAt, and verify.mts requires every date to be a real day and the top-level date to be the later of the two Internet.nl dates.
